findings.title: Refund rate KPI computable from DB but NOT exposed on owner-night dashboard
findings.details: Mission asks 'Refund rate' as one of owner-night POS questions. CORRECTION over first-read: refund infrastructure DOES exist via NF525 counter-entry mirror-order pattern (app/Services/Order/RefundWithCounterEntryService.php + POST /admin/pos/orders/{order}/refund-with-counter-entry route, api.php:961). Refunds materialize as full mirror Order rows with status=OrderStatus::RETURNED (=22), payment_status=PaymentStatus::REFUNDED (=20), negative total/subtotal/tax_amount, parent_order_id pointing to source order, AND audit_log action 'order.refund.counter_entry' (per service docstring). So refund-rate CAN be SQL-computed: COUNT(distinct orders WHERE status=22 AND payment_status=20) / COUNT(orders WHERE payment_status=5 settled) over period. HOWEVER: NO dashboard endpoint exposes this. Searched dashboard endpoints (total-orders, sales-summary, order-statistics, realtime-report, channel-statistics, sla-alerts, audit-trail, channel-statistics) — none returns refund_rate or refund_count fields. Owner reading EOD dashboard cannot see refund rate even though data exists in DB.
findings.evidence: State 4 refund_rate_today (initial mis-read corrected); RefundWithCounterEntryService.php line 25-189 docstring + insert pattern; OrderStatus::RETURNED=22 + PaymentStatus::REFUNDED=20 enum constants; routes/api.php:961 refund route; today's DB count = 0 RETURNED orders, 0 negative-total orders, 0 refund.* audit_logs
findings.impact: Owner cannot get refund-rate metric tonight from dashboard. Data IS queryable via direct SQL but no widget surfaces it. Workaround for owner: use sales-report/index with status filter (=22 RETURNED) — partial workaround. Common SaaS KPI (refund rate > X% triggers operational review) not surfaced to owner.
findings.fix_hint: EITHER (a) add a DashboardController::refundRate(period) endpoint that returns {refund_orders_count, total_orders_count, refund_rate_pct, refunded_amount_eur_abs} querying mirror-orders WHERE status=22 + payment_status=20 + DATE(created_at) range — read-only widget, no schema change required — and surface on owner-night EOD dashboard, OR (b) extend sales-report/overview response with refund_count + refund_amount + refund_rate fields. (a) is cleanest — preserves NF525 append-only discipline, no schema delta, ~30 LOC controller + service + frontend widget. F02 is P1 widget-missing, NOT P0 schema-missing — corrects this report's first-read.

findings.title: sales-report ?source_surface=<value> silently ignored — only numeric ?source= filter works
findings.details: GET /api/admin/sales-report?branch_id=1&source_surface=pos returns 2 rows (kiosk #63 + delivery #1, ALL orders) instead of 0 (no POS sales today or ever). Root cause: app/Services/OrderService.php $orderFilter allow-list (lines 65-82) contains 'source' but NOT 'source_surface'. The filter loop at line 162-192 ignores unknown keys silently. Numeric source filter (?source=2 for POS, ?source=5 for kiosk) works correctly — verified ?source=2 returns 0 rows, ?source=5 returns 1 row (#63). Owner UI dispatching the string 'source_surface' form (e.g. tabs labeled 'POS / Kiosk / Delivery') would silently fetch all-source data and display wrong per-surface totals to owner. No 422 / no warning.
findings.evidence: State 2 endpoints_hit (?source_surface=pos returns 2 orders); State 4 filter_drift_discovered with OrderService line-number anchors; State 5 adversarial_check_3
findings.impact: P2 because workaround exists (use numeric source). Risk surface: any owner-facing per-surface tab/widget that uses the string form would mis-display. Audit of frontend dispatching code recommended.
findings.fix_hint: EITHER (a) add 'source_surface' to OrderService::$orderFilter + applyOrderFilter handles string match on enum ('pos'|'kiosk'|'web'|'delivery'), OR (b) document API contract that only numeric ?source= is supported and audit frontend code (grep resources/js for ?source_surface= dispatches) to migrate to numeric, OR (c) emit a deprecation warning header when source_surface is sent. (a) is owner-friendliest (matches the human-readable column name) and one-block change in OrderService.
